issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must establish continuous readiness and willingness to perform the plaintiff’s contractual obligations.
material_facts: The purchaser knew of the mortgage when the later sale agreement was made.

The agreement required completion by a specified deadline, but the purchaser took no steps toward completion around that deadline and there was a substantial period before the next payment and communication.
The purchaser did not establish that he had performed the later proposed arrangement to pay the bank and the seller; the seller independently paid the bank.
The purchaser’s general assertion of readiness was not supported by evidence of continuous steps to complete the transaction.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser failed to prove continuous readiness and willingness, so the specific-performance suit had to be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires a plaintiff seeking specific performance to plead and prove readiness and willingness to perform the essential contractual terms continuously from the contract through the hearing. The Court relied on Gomathinayagam Pillai v. Pallaniswami Nadar, which quoted Ardeshir Mama v. Flora Sassoon, and J.P. Builders v. A. Ramadas Rao, including its statement that the burden rests on the plaintiff.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a suit asking a court to compel completion of a sale agreement.
predicates.purchaser_knew_of_encumbrance: The purchaser knew of an encumbrance affecting the property when entering the operative sale agreement.
predicates.completion_deadline_passed_without_compl: The contractual completion deadline passed without the purchaser taking steps toward completion.
predicates.purchaser_did_not_perform_later_payment_: The purchaser did not carry out the proposed later arrangement for paying the outstanding amounts to the seller and the creditor.

issues.definition: When a purchaser who knew of the encumbrance lets the completion deadline pass without taking steps and does not perform the later payment arrangement, the purchaser is denied specific performance for failure to prove continuous readiness.

issues.legal_issue: An inaccurate assurance that property is unencumbered does not justify summarily rejecting the seller’s defence as false when the purchaser knew of the encumbrance by the time of the operative agreement.
material_facts: The seller had earlier represented that the property was unencumbered, although it was mortgaged.
The same recital appeared in the later agreement, but the purchaser’s communication recorded that the encumbrance was known when that agreement was made.
The High Court treated the seller’s defence as wholly false and relied on S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jaganath to reject it.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to summarily reject the seller’s defence on that basis, and reliance on S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu was misplaced.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jaganath because it did not arise from a suit for specific performance and involved a plaintiff found to have withheld relevant documents. In this case, the purchaser’s knowledge of the encumbrance when making the operative agreement meant that the purchaser could not later assert the contrary; the earlier inaccurate recital did not warrant summarily rejecting the seller’s entire defence.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A purchaser brought a suit asking a court to compel completion of a sale agreement.
predicates.seller_made_inaccurate_no_encumbrance_re: The seller represented that the property was unencumbered even though it was subject to an encumbrance.
predicates.purchaser_knew_of_encumbrance_at_operati: The purchaser knew of the encumbrance when the operative agreement was made.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, an inaccurate no-encumbrance representation does not by itself justify summarily rejecting the seller’s defence when the purchaser knew of the encumbrance under the operative agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A vendor may recover possession on a counterclaim when the purchaser remains in possession without completing the sale or establishing entitlement to specific performance.
material_facts: The purchaser was in possession of the property, although the parties disputed how possession had been obtained.
The sale was not completed, and the purchaser did not establish performance of the payment obligations associated with the proposed arrangement for possession.
The vendor sought recovery of possession by counterclaim.
issues.conclusion: The counterclaim was allowed and the purchaser was required to deliver vacant and peaceful possession to the vendor.
issues.legal_principle: The Court allowed the vendor’s counterclaim for possession after rejecting the purchaser’s claim to specific performance and finding that the purchaser had not established performance of the obligations associated with the transaction. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this ruling.

rule.if: possession_counterclaim and purchaser_in_possession and sale_not_completed and specific_performance_denied

predicates.possession_counterclaim: A vendor counterclaimed for recovery of the property from a purchaser in possession.
predicates.purchaser_in_possession: The purchaser was in possession of the property.
predicates.sale_not_completed: The agreed sale had not been completed by execution of a sale deed.
predicates.specific_performance_denied: The purchaser was not granted specific performance of the sale agreement.

issues.definition: When a purchaser remains in possession after an uncompleted sale and is denied specific performance, a vendor’s possession counterclaim results in the purchaser having to return the property.

issues.legal_issue: The parties’ competing claims for mesne profits and interest on the advance may be equitably adjusted where the vendor retained the advance while the purchaser’s wrongful possession deprived the vendor of the property’s earnings.
material_facts: The purchaser had paid substantial advances, which the vendor retained.
The purchaser remained in wrongful possession and the vendor was deprived of the property’s earnings for a prolonged period.
The claim that the property generated annual income was not disputed.
The Court directed repayment of the advance but denied both interest on that sum and mesne profits for the period of wrongful possession.
issues.conclusion: The advance was refundable without interest, and the vendor was not entitled to mesne profits for the period of wrongful possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made an equitable adjustment in the circumstances: the vendor had retained the advance while being deprived of the property’s earnings, so neither party was awarded the additional monetary claim of interest on the advance or mesne profits. No earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this adjustment.

predicates.vendor_retained_substantial_advance: The vendor retained a substantial advance paid by the purchaser under the sale agreement.
predicates.purchaser_wrongfully_possessed_property: The purchaser remained in possession of the property without a completed sale or established right to specific performance.
predicates.vendor_was_deprived_of_property_earnings: The vendor was deprived of earnings that the property would otherwise have generated during the purchaser’s possession.

issues.definition: When the vendor retains a substantial advance and the purchaser’s wrongful possession deprives the vendor of property earnings, the advance is refunded without interest and mesne profits are denied.

issues.legal_issue: Interest may be imposed on a refund if the person ordered to refund it does not pay within the time fixed by the court.
material_facts: The Court ordered the vendor to refund the advance within a period fixed in its judgment.
The Court directed that interest would apply if the refund was not made within that period.
issues.conclusion: If the refund was not paid within the court-fixed period, it would carry interest from the expiry of that period.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly made interest conditional on non-payment within the time allowed for refund; no earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this direction.

predicates.refund_ordered: A court directed a party to repay money to another party.
predicates.refund_not_paid_within_court_fixed_perio: The party ordered to repay did not pay within the period fixed by the court.

issues.definition: When a court orders a refund and it is not paid within the time the court allows, the delayed refund carries interest.
